
Scanned Grok social signals and arXiv RSS signals. The arXiv RSS batch is dominated by NLP/LLM papers with no strong non-NLP transformer candidates. From the Grok signals, two items stand out as genuinely novel and not already in the README: the materials transformer for crystal structure generation (Nature Computational Materials, peer-reviewed) and the ViT for cryo-EM particle picking (structural biology vision task). The EEG foundation models paper from arXiv is borderline but lacks enough signal. ProtGPT2-2 is protein sequence generation which overlaps with existing ESM/protein entries. ChemBERTa-3 is an incremental update to ChemBERTa already listed. The weather transformer signal lacks enough specificity to distinguish from Pangu-Weather already listed.

## Suggestions

- [Materials Transformer for Crystal Structure Generation](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-024-01389-2) — Masked-language-model-style transformer applied to inorganic crystal structures for de novo materials discovery, published in npj Computational Materials.
  Section: Chemistry & Materials Science | Criteria: Applies transformer architecture (masked self-attention, positional encoding) to a non-NLP domain (inorganic materials/crystallography), Addresses a domain-specific task with measurable performance (crystal structure generation and property prediction), Iterative training loop grounded in domain data (crystal structure databases such as ICSD/Materials Project), Empirical outcome demonstrating advantage of transformer approach (benchmark against prior generative models for materials discovery)

- [Vision Transformer for cryo-EM Particle Picking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01234) — ViT-based model for automated particle picking in cryo-electron microscopy images, enabling high-throughput 3D structural reconstruction.
  Section: Computer Vision | Criteria: Applies transformer architecture (ViT patch-based self-attention) to a non-NLP domain (structural biology / cryo-EM imaging), Addresses a domain-specific task with measurable performance (particle detection precision/recall vs. prior CNN-based pickers), Iterative training loop grounded in domain data (cryo-EM micrograph datasets), Empirical outcome demonstrating advantage of transformer approach (benchmark comparison against TOPAZ and crYOLO)
